purpose: Define piloted and optionally autonomous machines for combat, research, construction, rescue, and extraction across terrestrial, aquatic, subsurface, atmospheric, orbital, and space environments.
governingPrinciple: A mech is a configured physical machine, not a humanoid silhouette with arbitrary hit points.

warfareEvolution.label: Terrestrial industrial warfare
warfareEvolution.lesson: Wheels, tracks, legs, and specialized machinery compete by terrain, payload, cost, and repairability.

warfareEvolution.label: Powered personal systems
warfareEvolution.lesson: Augmentation scales the person; it does not automatically make a person-sized system a tank.

warfareEvolution.label: Remote and autonomous systems
warfareEvolution.lesson: Remote operation trades onboard crew exposure for communications, autonomy, latency, and electronic-warfare constraints.

warfareEvolution.label: Atmospheric and orbital specialization
warfareEvolution.lesson: Pressure, radiation, thermal management, reaction control, and anchoring dominate many tasks.

warfareEvolution.label: Space-industrial platforms
warfareEvolution.lesson: Human-compatible manipulators can help around human-built structures; momentum and restraint remain mandatory.

warfareEvolution.label: Return to exotic environments
warfareEvolution.lesson: Specialized locomotion and sealed bodies return where terrain or inherited infrastructure rewards them.

platformFamilies.purpose: Pilotable combat machine with locomotion, manipulators, protection, sensors, weapons, and egress.
Lifting, construction, casualty recovery, and field repair.
Sensors, sampling, drilling, and hazardous exploration.
Cut, bore, collect, sort, and transfer material.
Hull work, module alignment, and wreck recovery in orbit or space.
Operate in deep ocean, caverns, dense atmospheres, cryogenic or volcanic terrain, and unusual gravity.

combatRules: Weapons have physical mounts, arcs, recoil, heat, ammunition, reload, and interlocks.
Hits resolve against armor, joints, sensors, actuators, cables, weapons, and internal systems rather than one health bar.
A damaged limb changes mobility or balance; a damaged sensor creates a blind sector; a damaged feed can make ammunition unavailable.
A mech can be degraded, immobilized, abandoned, captured, repaired, or salvaged without being destroyed.
Pilot egress, injury, rescue, recovery, and capture are part of combat.

prototypeFailureExamples: foot placement fails on loose regolith
salvage rig spins after cutting a loaded member

validationGates: Walking combat mechs are an explicit desired player capability.
Combat, research, construction, rescue, and extraction share engineering rules but have different mission contracts.
Mass, power, heat, terrain, stability, recoil, maintenance, and qualification constrain operation.
Space rigs account for momentum, anchoring, tethers, and reaction control.
Prototype failures and repairs persist as world history.
Evolution branches; no platform is universally optimal.

pilotExperience.principle: The player operates the mech by boarding and inhabiting its physical pilot station; a mech is not a camera mode or a remote avatar unless that configuration explicitly is remote-operated.

motionInterface.concept: A qualified pilot may use a motion-capture harness or instrumented control frame to map body posture and gestures to mech commands.
rules: Pilot movement is an input signal, not an instruction to teleport machine limbs into the same pose.
The machine's actuators, balance controller, traction, load, damage, and terrain determine the achieved motion.
The harness can be absent, degraded, bypassed, or incompatible; manual controls remain a separately specified control path.

interfaceSemantics.oneAuthoritativeWorldObject: Desktop, VR hand/controller, mouse, keyboard, and accessibility inputs invoke the same semantic action against the same physical control or system.
interfaceSemantics.feedbackMustReflect: actual subsystem state, command acceptance, latency, interlocks, power, connectivity, damage, and stale data
rules: A command request is not proof that a mechanism moved or a system changed state.
Physical reach, line of sight where relevant, access authority, and current machine condition constrain interaction.
Accessibility mappings may change the input device without bypassing world-state rules.

damageableInterfaces.rule: A shot resolves against physical geometry and intervening construction; a hit does not magically disable every connected subsystem.

renderingPerformanceContract.principle: Treat pixels, memory, bandwidth, synchronization, and device limits as measurable budgets. GPU-side state and rendering can scale far beyond per-object CPU draw submission, but never imply literally unlimited capacity.
candidateArchitecture: separate authoritative simulation state from presentation caches
share mesh and material definitions across instances
use instancing, batching, indirect draws, and GPU-driven visibility where the target API supports them
join static geometry selectively when it reduces overhead without harming culling, updates, damage, or material boundaries
retain independently addressable components for animated joints, articulated equipment, collision, damage, repair, and salvage
use hierarchical visibility, level of detail, screen-space error, and event-horizon fidelity tiers
partition render and state data into pages or tiles with explicit capacity and residency policy
keep CPU-readable semantic state for gameplay, interaction, persistence, and diagnosis; GPU buffers are not the only authoritative record
measuredLimits: target resolution, refresh rate, and frame-time budget

joinWhen: geometry is static or changes as one unit
components share compatible materials and visibility
joint update and damage granularity are not required
keepSeparateWhen: parts can be independently damaged, hidden, repaired, replaced, or salvaged
separate culling or LOD is valuable
material, transparency, collision, or interaction boundaries matter
meshJoiningPolicy.requirement: Benchmark representative scenes on target hardware; do not choose joining or GPU residency from theory alone.

benchmarkScenarios: one mech with articulated limbs, cockpit controls, and local damage
a squad of visually distinct mechs sharing chassis assets
large formation with repeated components and per-instance state
damage, debris, and salvage changing visibility during combat
VR stereo rendering at target refresh rate
low-end integrated GPU and high-end discrete GPU
cold load, warm cache, memory pressure, and device recovery
reportMetrics: CPU frame time and submission time
GPU frame time and pass breakdown
frame-time percentiles and missed refresh deadlines
validationRules: No capacity claim is accepted without a reproducible workload and target hardware.
Pixel count is one budget among geometry, bandwidth, memory, synchronization, and simulation costs.
GPU optimization must not erase semantic identity, physical interaction, or damageable component boundaries.
VR comfort and target refresh deadlines are measured separately from average throughput.
GPU state textures are caches or packed state planes unless a contract explicitly makes them authoritative and defines recovery/persistence.
Performance improvements are checked against visual correctness, interaction latency, and persistent damage behavior.
